body:
Deal: Energizer Extreme AA Rechargeable 2300mAh 4-Pack Batteries $10.79 ($9.71 Sub & Save) + Delivery ($0 with Prime/$59+) @ Amazon AU

[rav99] If I don't have a charger what's the best way to get one? I see the charger has 4 included batteries?
[HeyJes] Same. Issue is I don’t have the charger….
[Skinnerr] Ikea cheapo one or a Liito Kala from Aliexpress.
[Lone star] Any electricians help me out please. I have this solar security light which uses rechargeable AA 2000mAh 1.2V. One of the 3 batteries died so I bought a 4 pack Energizer AA rechargeable 2300mAh 1.2V from Bunnings. For some damn reason those Energizer batteries would not work on the solar security light. The difference I can tell is 2000mAh and 2300mAh. Why is it not compatible?
[RecklessMonkeys] Bit of a guess, but the voltage may not be up enough.
[Lone star] Hmm.. I will to find out how the check the voltage on both of brands then.
[Aldonis] shouldn't matter. mah is just the available reserve of power to draw from, the Energizer has a higher capacity is all
[Lone star] With my poor knowledge in electricity, I also was aware of that.. But yet don't understand why the Energizer batteries didn't work on the solar light. 🤔
[Jackson] standard non-rechargeable AA batteries are 1.5V each, while nimh are 1.2V each. Stacking 3 together in series makes it 4.5V to 3.6V, almost a whole volt less. Most devices will just work but some either require the full voltage or have some circuitry to cut power if the voltage drops below a certain level. What you should do is charge them fully in a separate charger and then put them in, if they don't work then they are never going to work.
I have this issue with an old digital camera of mine which used to have 750mah removable Li-ion battery that you could purchase separately. When this LRV3 battery shat it I wasn't able to get another one easily, so I tried my 2450mah Ladda batteries, and while the camera works for a few shots it still turns off after only a couple of minutes. I'm probably going to have to buy Li-ion AA batteries but they are a fair bit more expensive
[Lone star] Hi. It made me very very curious why the Energizer batteries didn't work. The batteries which came with the solar light are 2000mAh 1.2V and Energizer is 2300mAh 1.2V. Both brands are 1.2V. In theory that would work.
[Jackson] In theory, but in reality they may have a lower voltage or not hold the 1.2v for more than a short period after charge. It could also be a faulty battery or the device itself could be faulty. Sometimes running a device at the wrong voltage (even under) could cause an issue with it. Shouldn't happen with a quality product but that's life these days
[Lone star] @Jackson: You know what's strange. After I charged the 2 (original) still working batteries and plug in the solar light with the almost dead (3rd battery). It actually works, but because it only can give out about 1.0% capacity, the light only can function about 5% or less of it's actually 100%.. You know what I mean?
[Lone star] FYI. The battery packet is stated "pre-charged", but it wasn't in my situation. It was only around 46% charged.
[snensnay] Will my nitecore charger charge these? The one I use for eneloops.
[A female dog] If JB $10 perks vouchers are still being offered - might be worth price matching and and getting this item for $0.79.
[dufflover] Pay extra for LADDAs IMO. In my experience these are not any better (if not worse) than typical Chinese made NiMH low self discharge batteries like the rebadged Liitokalas or Amazon Basics.
[IlIlIl IlI llIIIl] I have some old ones of these and they no longer work compared to other cheapo rechargeables. Not sure it's worth paying a premium over cheap alternatives
